title: English Practice Test 1 - English - Knowledge of Language
subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice most effectively maintains the essay’s tone?

 Careful harvesting ensures that the tree will **live to yield** more hearts, resulting in environmentally friendly production.
questions.explain: The original phrasing maintains the formal and informational tone of the essay, avoiding the overly colloquial phrasing found in the other options.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is least redundant in context?

 Atala prioritizes his working relationships with Amazonian tribes. Utilizing their historical **know-how they have**, he aims to bolster tribe members’ livelihoods while exposing a wider audience to Brazilian ingredients.
options: knowledge that tribe members know about local plants,
knowledge of local plants in the area,
questions.explain: 'knowledge of local plants' provides the necessary information in the most concise way, removing the repetitive 'know-how they have' or redundancy present in the other options.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is clearest and most precise in context?

 Expanding awareness of the rich diversity of Brazil’s native ingredients, Atala continues to lead in **deciphering** the country’s food culture. With his characteristic passion and intensity, the renowned chef seeks to inspire Brazilians to rediscover the connections between culture, nature, and food.
questions.explain: 'transforming' is the most precise word choice here because the passage discusses Atala innovating and changing the global perception of Brazil's food culture, which makes 'transforming' highly appropriate over deciphering, dislocating, or contorting.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice most effectively maintains the essay’s tone?

 Her title did not require a vow of poverty, but Hrosvitha did take the abbey’s customary vow of chastity, which absolved her of an obligation to marry. This circumstance **made it okay for her to keep her** financial status without incurring responsibilities to a husband and children.
options: permitted her to hang on to
questions.explain: 'Allowed her to retain' is the only phrase that matches the academic and formal tone established in the rest of the historical essay.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is least redundant in context?

 When we’re nearly three miles into our detour, I roll down the windows. **Looking pointedly into the rearview mirror, windows rolled down,** I say something about not throwing anything out of the car, but neither boy is listening.
options: into the rearview mirror, three miles into our detour,
behind me by looking into the rearview mirror,
questions.explain: The context right before this states 'I roll down the windows.' Therefore, repeating 'windows rolled down' or details about the detour is redundant. Option d is concise and avoids redundancy.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is least redundant in context?

 I’ve been taking this detour out of Albuquerque for two years, ever since these musical rumble strips **were installed**.
options: that play music were put in.
were added a couple years ago.
questions.explain: The original text ('were installed') is concise and sufficient. The other options uselessly repeat facts already established in the sentence ('out of Albuquerque', 'for two years', or 'musical').
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is clearest and most precise in context?

 **Whereas** a museum designates areas for visible storage, it uses space efficiently, providing safe displays for artifacts and allowing visitors greater access to independently study the works that make the museum unique.
questions.explain: The conjunction "When" sets up the correct cause-and-effect / temporal relationship. It clearly states the positive consequences that occur "when" a museum designates areas for visible storage.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice is least redundant in context?

 In each chamber, up to five of the sparrow-sized birds can huddle **as a group together when the Kalahari nights get cold**.
options: all together, staying warm when the temperature drops and gets colder at night.
and stay warm when temperatures plummet at night and it’s cold.
for warmth during the cold Kalahari nights.
questions.explain: The word "huddle" already implies gathering together. Options a, b, and c are all overly wordy and repetitive. Option d succinctly states why they are huddling ("for warmth during the cold Kalahari nights").
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which choice best maintains the stylistic pattern of descriptions established earlier in the sentence?

 She depicts flowers with layers of petals, intricate spirals and rosettes, teardrops bending within circles, and **dizzying mazes of lines**—embroidering them in vibrant reds, blues, pinks, yellows, and greens...
questions.explain: The prior items in the series are vivid, noun-based descriptive phrases ("layers of petals," "intricate spirals"). "Dizzying mazes of lines" matches this specific poetic rhythm and structure perfectly.
questions.subject: English
